prize_parts.citation: For the invention and realization of optical lattice clocks based on magic-wavelength trapping, taking optical frequency standards to the 10^-18 level

statement.case_for: The optical lattice clock is a single, sharply defined invention: Katori's magic-wavelength idea removes the light-shift problem that would otherwise prevent trapping many atoms without perturbing the clock transition, and the realization by Katori and by Ye's group took fractional uncertainty to the 10^-18 range. That changed what can be measured, which is the criterion I weigh most heavily. Five of eight members placed it in their top three, and the support is broad rather than concentrated in one subfield: Lindroth ranked it first, and Danielsson, Eriksson, Olsson, Pearce and Mehlig all rank it within their top five. Several independent laboratories (Tokyo, JILA, PTB, NIST, SYRTE and others) reproduce and compare clocks at this level, the interpretation is stable, and the payoffs (the SI second redefinition roadmap, tests of constants, relativistic geodesy) are concrete. The attribution is the cleanest on the shortlist: two names, a clear originator and a clear driver of record performance, and the 2005 comb prize to Hall and Hansch is a separate achievement on which the clocks build.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservations are that the formal redefinition of the second has not happened, so some of the claimed impact is prospective, and that a 'lattice clock' prize risks understating other contributors (other Sr and Yb groups, and the ultrastable-laser and comb infrastructure) whose names are outside the credited pair. There is also a fair point that B001 has more first-place support, four first places against two, and a larger scientific and community footprint than a metrology invention. If the committee's central criterion were breadth of influence on physics rather than an enabling measurement capability, B001 would rightly rank above B007, and my own opening ranking put it only fourth partly because the superconducting mechanism is unsettled, not because the discovery is in doubt.

responses.point: Danielsson ranks B001 first as a clean prediction-then-experiment case (Bistritzer-MacDonald flat bands, then the 2018 correlated-insulator and superconducting states), reproduced widely and not premature after eight years.
responses.response: I accept the quality of the sequence and the independent reproduction, and I have moved B001 from a distant fourth to my first alternative. My disagreement is about maturity and settled content. The physical interpretation of the superconducting and correlated phases is still debated, and the field is evolving fast, whereas the lattice clock is a finished capability with stable interpretation and multi-laboratory comparison at the 10^-18 level. The three-name split also forces choices between the Jarillo-Herrero experimental group and other experimental groups (Dean, Efetov, Young, Yazdani) that the clock pair does not face. I do not read four first places as a larger scientific margin than the broad top-three support for B007.

responses.point: Eriksson ranks B001 first because a simple theory predicted a precise quantitative condition that experiment then confirmed, and notes that the superconducting mechanism remains debated; he ranks B007 fifth with a clear idea and concrete impact.
responses.response: I agree that the quantitative magic-angle prediction is unusual and persuasive. Where I differ is that the clock offers the same prediction-then-confirmation structure in measurement form: magic-wavelength trapping was proposed to cancel light shifts and was then shown to work at progressively smaller uncertainties. I would ask Olle whether placing B007 fifth reflects a metrology bias in valuing capability over discovery, or a specific attribution concern, since he calls the Katori-Ye pair well separated from the 2005 prize. If it is the former, we are weighing different things, and I think the record of enabling new measurements in physics is a legitimate and long-standing basis for the prize.

responses.point: Johansson ranks B058 (circuit QED) first, with high originality and industrial-scale impact, while openly flagging his proximity to superconducting circuits and noting that Wallraff is omitted from the credited names.
responses.response: I credit Johansson for declaring his proximity, and I share his attribution concern: a prize on circuit QED without Wallraff would be hard to defend, and the three-name limit cannot accommodate it fairly alongside Blais, Girvin and Schoelkopf. That is my main reason for not placing B058 in my preferred configuration. The 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in superconducting circuits also overlaps in subject and may make a further circuits award in short order less compelling. If the committee reopens B058 with a different credited set, I would listen, but on the supplied names B007 is a more defensible configuration.

responses.point: Olsson ranks B030 (aberration-corrected electron optics, Rose, Haider, Urban) first as a clear, well-defined invention with routine sub-angstrom imaging and a mature, commercial footprint.
responses.response: I agree that B030 is the same kind of instrument-enabling invention that I value, and that its attribution and maturity are strong. Only Olsson ranked it, however, and it appears only once in the opening ballots, so in the supported record it has far less breadth than B007. I would be interested in her view on whether B030 is better treated as an instrumentation prize with strong materials-science impact or as a physics discovery, and whether its impact is mainly in materials science and chemistry rather than fundamental physics. I would not object to B030 in a two-part configuration, but I do not see it displacing B007 as the lead.

responses.point: Mehlig ranks B001 first but would limit the credit to MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero as the cleanest configuration, noting that this leaves Bistritzer out.
responses.response: The attribution issue Bernhard raises for B001 is exactly the kind that makes me cautious. Bistritzer and MacDonald co-authored the continuum-model prediction, so dropping Bistritzer to reach a pair is difficult to justify, while including him leaves no room for other experimental contributors. By comparison B007 reaches a defensible two-person credit with little controversy. I note Mehlig ranks B007 fourth, so he sees it as sound; if his concern is topical rather than scientific, I would accept B001 as the committee's alternative lead.

uncertainties: How much weight the committee should give to the not-yet-completed redefinition of the second when judging maturity of B007.

Whether credit between Katori's magic-wavelength concept and Ye's later performance and many-body milestones will be seen as co-equal, and whether other Sr and Yb lattice-clock groups have a claim the three-name limit cannot accommodate.
Whether the committee will prefer B001's larger first-place support over B007's broader top-three support, and whether the unsettled superconducting mechanism weighs against B001 timing.
I rely on memory rather than checked sources for the latest clock uncertainty figures and for the details of the 2005 and 2025 prizes.
statement.conflict_note: My profile documents a research stay in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder during my doctoral period, and Jun Ye is closely associated with Hall and JILA, the laureate and group at the centre of B007's credited pair. This is a possible personal and institutional connection and may call for recusal or at least explicit disclosure on B007. I also have a field proximity to atomic physics and quantum optics, including quantum-memory and quantum-information work in Lund, which touches B015 and B008 and could bias my views of them. I have no documented link to Katori.
